_comment: Instrument Tier 1 — intake, the 11 category gates, and the 21 path activation rules. SPEC §3.1/§3.2, G-27 (wording is the owner's), G-50 (pilot depth), G-35, G-36, G-38. Versioned data: immutable once activated (§5.7). Changing this is a governance event, never a code change.

sections.title: What are you doing?
sections.help: Two or three sentences in your own words. This is the only place you describe the activity, and every question after it is shaped by what you write here.

fields.help: The name your team uses for it. It does not need to be an official project code.

fields.text: In your own words, what is this activity and what will it do?
fields.help: Say what it does, who uses it, what data it touches and who else is involved. Detail here saves you questions later — this is the one answer the whole assessment reads from.

fields.text: When do you expect this to go live?
fields.help: An approximate date is fine. This is used to sequence review, not to judge the activity.

sections.title: Who owns it?
sections.help: The people a reviewer would contact. Choose from the list; if someone is missing you can still type them in.

fields.text: Who is accountable for this activity?
fields.help: The person who would answer for it at a governance forum — usually not the person filling this in.

fields.text: Which part of the business is this for?
fields.help: The unit that benefits from the activity, not the unit building it.

fields.text: Who can answer technical questions about it?
fields.help: Leave blank if that is you.

sections.title: What kind of activity is it?
sections.help: Four facts about your own project. Nothing here is a classification against our taxonomy — G-20.

fields.text: Is this something new, or a change to something that already exists?
fields.help: A change still needs assessing — what changed is what we look at.

options.label: A change to something we already run

fields.text: Is there an earlier assessment for the thing you are changing?
fields.help: A name or reference is enough. Leave blank if you do not know of one — we will look.

fields.text: Does this activity use AI or machine learning in any form?
fields.help: That includes a model you build, a model you call, and an AI feature inside a product you buy. If you are not sure, say so — someone will confirm it with you.

fields.text: What does the AI actually do here?
fields.help: One sentence. For example: drafts a reply a person then sends, or scores an application and passes it to an underwriter.

fields.text: Is a third party involved in delivering this — a vendor, a supplier, a partner?
fields.help: Answer No if everything is built and run in-house. An empty vendor box proves nothing, which is why we ask (G-35).
Choose from the list of vendors we already hold. If yours is not there, type it — it will be recorded against this assessment and reviewed before it joins the shared list.

sections.title: What data and obligations are in play?
sections.help: Two questions. Both change what you are asked next, so they are worth a moment.

fields.text: What is the most sensitive data involved?
fields.help: Pick the highest band that applies, even if most of the data sits below it. The descriptions place almost any case.

options.label: Public
options.description: Already published, or fine to publish. No harm if it were seen outside the organisation.

options.label: Internal
options.description: Ordinary business information. Not for outside, but no specific harm from a single leak.

options.label: Confidential
options.description: Personal information, commercial terms, or anything where exposure would harm a person or a deal.

options.label: Restricted
options.description: The most sensitive we hold — special category personal data, credentials, material non-public information.

fields.text: Has anything been bought or signed yet?
fields.help: An honest No is useful. It tells a reviewer whether there is still room to change terms.

gate.text: Does this activity involve a third party — a vendor, supplier, partner or contractor?
gate.help: Anyone outside the organisation who builds, hosts, operates or supports part of this activity.

prefill_from.reason: You told us a third party is involved when you described the activity.

gate.text: Does this activity use AI, machine learning or an automated model to produce an output?
gate.help: Including a model inside a product you buy, and a model you call through an API.

prefill_from.reason: You told us this activity uses AI when you described it.

gate.text: Does this activity handle information about people?
gate.help: Customers, employees, candidates, patients — anyone. Including information you only pass through.

prefill_from.reason: You told us the most sensitive data involved is Confidential or Restricted.

gate.text: Does this activity involve a system that stores, processes or transmits our data?
gate.help: Almost any technology activity does. Answer No only for something with no system component at all.

categories.name: Solution Architecture

gate.text: Does this activity introduce or change a system's architecture?
gate.help: New components, new integrations, a new hosting arrangement, a change to how data flows.

categories.boundary_note: Yes records this area's scope for a reviewer and asks nothing further in the pilot. Architecture depth arrives with the next instrument version; recording it now is what puts it in front of the right reviewer.

categories.name: Legal, Regulatory & Compliance

gate.text: Is this activity subject to a specific law, regulation or contractual obligation?
gate.help: If you are not sure, say so — the legal and compliance offices would rather confirm than have you guess.

categories.boundary_note: Yes routes this to the compliance office with what you have already told us, and asks nothing further in the pilot.

categories.name: Operational Risk

gate.text: Does this activity change how a business process runs day to day?
gate.help: A new step, a removed step, a task that moves from a person to a system.

categories.boundary_note: Yes records the process change for a reviewer and asks nothing further in the pilot.

categories.name: Governance & Oversight

gate.text: Governance & Oversight applies to every activity.
gate.help: This is not a question. Every activity has an accountable owner and a decision record, so this area is recorded as applying and is not counted in what is left for you to do (G-36).

categories.boundary_note: Applies · not asked. Recorded as in scope for a reviewer; nothing here is yours to answer.

categories.name: Ethics & Conduct

gate.text: Could this activity affect people in a way they would object to if they knew?
gate.help: Differential treatment, surveillance, a decision made about someone without their knowledge. An honest Yes is not an admission — it is what gets a specialist involved early.

categories.boundary_note: Yes records the concern in your own words for the ethics reviewer and asks nothing further in the pilot. This area deliberately stops here rather than putting a rubric between you and a specialist.

categories.name: People & Capacity

gate.text: Does this activity depend on people or skills we do not currently have?
gate.help: New hires, a new specialism, or a team already at capacity.

categories.boundary_note: Yes records the dependency for a reviewer and asks nothing further in the pilot.

categories.name: Jurisdiction-Bound Execution

gate.text: Will any part of this activity be carried out from, or its data held in, another country?
gate.help: Where the work happens and where the data sits, not where the vendor is headquartered.

categories.boundary_note: Yes records the jurisdictions for a reviewer and asks nothing further in the pilot; the data-transfer question itself is asked under Data & Privacy, where it routes.

tier1_questions.text: What will the third party do for you?
tier1_questions.help: Choose everything that applies. Each one opens a different set of questions, and choosing nothing here is not a way to skip them — it just means nobody knows what they do.

options.label: Connects to or logs in to our systems
Handles information about people on our behalf
Runs something we could not operate without
Uses their own suppliers to deliver part of it
Delivers the work from outside our home country

tier1_questions.text: How will the third party reach our systems?
tier1_questions.help: Only asked because you said they connect to or log in to our systems. If you do not know yet, hand this question off rather than guessing.

options.label: Their staff get their own named accounts
They share one account between people
They need administrator or privileged rights
System to system, over an API
Onto our network, over a VPN or a private link

tier1_questions.text: What does the AI do in this activity?
tier1_questions.help: Choose everything that applies. The difference between suggesting to a person and acting on its own is the single most important thing on this page.

options.label: Suggests something a person then decides
Drafts content a person reviews before it goes out
Makes a decision without a person in the loop
Takes actions in other systems on its own
Classifies, scores or ranks people or cases

tier1_questions.text: Where does the model come from?
tier1_questions.help: If a vendor's product does the AI part and you cannot see inside it, choose the vendor option — that is a real and common answer, not a gap.

options.label: We built and trained it ourselves
A commercial model we call through an API
An open-weights model we host ourselves
It is inside a product we buy, and we cannot see inside it

tier1_questions.text: What does the model see to do its job?
tier1_questions.help: What goes in at the point of use — prompts, retrieved documents, records from a database. Not what it was originally trained on.

options.label: Only information that is already public

tier1_questions.help: Choose everyone whose information this activity touches, including people who are not our customers.

tier1_questions.text: Does any of it fall into a specially protected category?
tier1_questions.help: Health, biometrics, genetics, race or ethnicity, religion, political opinions, trade union membership, sexual orientation, criminal records. If any of these appear even incidentally, say so.

options.label: Race, ethnicity, religion or political opinions

tier1_questions.text: Will information about people leave the country it is held in today?
tier1_questions.help: Including a vendor support team viewing it from another country. Viewing counts as a transfer.
Choose everything that applies. Anything reachable from the public internet is treated differently from something only reachable inside our network.

options.label: Customers log in to it directly
Partners call it over an API

tier1_questions.text: Who will hold administrator or privileged access?
tier1_questions.help: Privileged access means being able to change the system itself or read all of its data, not just use it.

options.label: Automated processes, using their own credentials

tier1_questions.text: How quickly would the business need this back after an outage?
tier1_questions.help: Your honest operational expectation, not an ambition. This sets what recovery evidence you will be asked for.

options.label: Longer than a week is tolerable
